erev0s/VAmPI.what: SQL injection in GET /users/v1/{username}: the username is formatted into a raw SELECT in User.get_user (models/user_model.py), called from get_by_username in api_views/users.py.

Unauthorized password change: PUT /users/v1/{username}/password lets any logged-in user overwrite the password of the user named in the URL with no owner check (update_password in api_views/users.py).
BOLA: GET /books/v1/{book} returns a book's secret to any logged-in user, not only its owner (get_by_title in api_views/books.py).
Mass assignment: POST /users/v1/register accepts an 'admin' field from the client and creates an admin account (register_user in api_views/users.py).

snoopysecurity/dvws-node.what: SQL injection in GET /api/v2/passphrase/:username: the username is concatenated into a raw SELECT (get in src/controllers/passphrase.js, routed in src/routes/passphrase.js).
SQL injection in POST /api/v2/passphrase: the passphrase and reminder fields are concatenated into a raw INSERT (save in src/controllers/passphrase.js).
NoSQL injection in POST /api/v2/notesearch: the search value is embedded in a MongoDB $where JavaScript expression (search_note in src/controllers/notes.js).
Mass assignment at registration: POST /api/v2/users passes req.body to new User(), so the client can set admin:true (add in src/controllers/users.js).

Mass assignment through the unauthenticated XML profile import: POST /api/v2/users/profile/import/xml accepts an <admin> element and writes it to the account (importProfileXml in src/controllers/users.js).
Mass assignment: PUT /api/v2/users/notification-preferences copies every submitted field onto the account, including admin (updateNotificationPreferences in src/controllers/integrations.js).

IDOR on notes: GET/PUT/DELETE /api/v2/notes/:noteId read, change or delete any user's note by its sequential id or name with no ownership check (read_a_note, update_a_note, delete_a_note in src/controllers/notes.js).
Horizontal access control: GET /api/v2/passphrase/:username returns any user's passphrases, with no authentication at all (get in src/controllers/passphrase.js).
Vertical access control: the admin-only GET /api/v2/users (all users including password hashes) works with a regular user's token (getAll in src/controllers/users.js).
Vertical access control: GET /api/v2/sysinfo/:command, which should be admin-only, works with a regular user's token (get_sysinfo in src/controllers/notes.js).
Vertical access control: the admin SOAP user lookup at POST /dvwsuserservice needs no authentication (src/services/soap/user-service.js).
XML XSS: POST /dvwsuserservice reflects the username into the SOAP response unescaped, so script runs if a client renders it with innerHTML (src/services/soap/user-service.js).
Content-Type XSS: POST /api/v2/users reflects the username in a text/plain response without X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff (add in src/controllers/users.js).
DOM XSS: the dashboard renders the URL hash through {@html} (frontend/src/routes/(app)/dashboard/+page.svelte).
Stored XSS: note responses and note bodies are rendered unsanitized through {@html} (frontend/src/routes/(app)/notes/+page.svelte, frontend/src/routes/(app)/search/+page.svelte).

XSS: login/register and admin error messages, which echo user input such as the username, are rendered through {@html} (frontend/src/routes/+page.svelte, frontend/src/routes/(app)/admin/+page.svelte).
GraphQL access control: the readNote(name) query returns any user's private notes to any token holder (src/graphql/schema.js).

GraphQL access control: userFindbyId (with an id from userSearchByUsername) returns another account's record, including its password hash and admin flag, to anonymous and regular callers with no ownership or role check (src/graphql/schema.js).

Broken object authorization: GET /api/v2/users/:id/profile-details checks the profile owner's admin flag instead of the caller's, so any user can read the admin account's email and home address by id (getUserProfileDetails in src/controllers/users.js).

Account recovery IDOR: POST /api/v2/account-recovery/reset sets a new password for any userId (found through POST /api/v2/account-recovery/lookup) with no ownership check or proof of recovery (resetAccountPassword in src/controllers/users.js).
Support ticket IDOR: GET /api/v2/support/tickets/:id returns another user's ticket because ownership is not checked (read in src/controllers/support-tickets.js).

Unrestricted file upload: POST /api/upload checks only that the name ends in .xml (no content check) and stores the file under the client's file name in the publicly served public/uploads/<username>/ (post in src/controllers/files.js; the frontend file input has no accept filter).
GraphQL updateUserUploadFile joins the client-supplied filePath to the upload directory unsanitized, so ../ writes the uploaded content anywhere on disk (src/graphql/schema.js).

Negative quantities: POST /api/v2/resource-store/orders accepts quantities down to -1000, and unitPrice x quantity then credits the wallet (src/routes/resource-store.js); this covers both Resource Store challenges.

cr0hn/vulnerable-node.what: BOLA: GET /orders/:id loads any order, including another customer's address and full card number, with no ownership check (routes/orders.js, orderById in model/db.js).
BOLA in the JSON API: GET /api/v1/orders?user_id= returns any user's orders (routes/api/v1.js, ordersForUser in model/db.js).
SQL injection login bypass: POST /login/auth concatenates the username into SQL (login in model/db.js, routes/auth.js).
UNION SQL injection: GET /search?q= concatenates q into the products query (searchProducts in model/db.js, routes/shop.js).
ORDER BY SQL injection: GET /orders?sort= is interpolated into the query (ordersForUserSorted in model/db.js).
NoSQL operator injection: POST /api/tags-filter passes user JSON such as {"$ne":null} straight into a Mongo query on product_meta (routes/shop.js).
NoSQL operator injection: GET /api/meta turns bracket query parameters (origin[$ne], origin[$regex]) into Mongo operators (routes/shop.js).
Mass assignment at signup: POST /register writes the whole request body to the user row, so role=admin and balance are accepted (routes/auth.js, views/register.ejs).
Mass assignment on profile update: POST /account accepts role and balance from the form (routes/account.js, updateProfile in model/db.js).
Stored XSS: review bodies posted to /products/:id/reviews (routes/shop.js) are rendered unescaped with <%- r.body %> (views/product_detail.ejs).
Price tampering: POST /checkout trusts the client's amount_cents and stores it as the charged amount (routes/orders.js, views/checkout.ejs, createOrder in model/db.js).
Committed secret: the API JWT signing secret jwt-super-secret is hardcoded in config.js (jwtSecret) and docker-compose.yml, so anyone with the repo can mint tokens.
SAST seed: SQL injection by string concatenation in queryUser (sast/seeds/sqli-concat.js).
SAST seed: NoSQL operator injection from user JSON in findUser (sast/seeds/nosql-operator.js).
SAST seed: reflected XSS in an HTML response in renderPage (sast/seeds/xss-raw-echo.js).
SAST seed: hardcoded API secret in getConfig (sast/seeds/hardcoded-secret.js).

anxolerd/dvpwa.what: SQL injection: POST /students/ formats the student name into an INSERT with % string formatting (Student.create in sqli/dao/student.py, via students in sqli/views.py).
Stored XSS: review text posted to /courses/{id}/review renders unescaped on /courses/{id} (sqli/templates/course.jinja2), because Jinja2 is set up with autoescape=False in sqli/app.py.

Stored XSS in other fields: student names and course titles/descriptions render unescaped (sqli/templates/students.jinja2, courses.jinja2, course.jinja2, evaluate.jinja2, review.jinja2; autoescape=False in sqli/app.py).

Missing function-level authorization: the admin-only POST /courses/ and POST /students/{student_id}/evaluate/{course_id} (plus POST /students/ and /courses/{id}/review) have no server-side check in sqli/views.py, because authorize(ensure_admin=True) from sqli/utils/auth.py is never used.

Access control: the admin-only GET /api/v1/approve-article/<article-id>/ can be run by non-admin users (approve_article in Tiredful-API/blog/views.py).
IDOR: GET /api/v1/exams/<exam_id>/ (base64 ids) returns other students' exam results (get_score in Tiredful-API/exams/views.py).
SQL injection (SQLite): the month field of POST /api/v1/activities/ is formatted into a raw query (get_activity in Tiredful-API/health/views.py).

dolevf/Damn-Vulnerable-GraphQL-Applicati.what: Stored XSS / HTML injection: the createPaste and importPaste mutations (core/views.py) accept any characters in the title and content, which then render as HTML on the public and private paste pages (templates/paste.html).
SQL injection: the filter argument of the pastes query is inserted into a raw SQL text() filter (resolve_pastes in core/views.py).

Upload stored under the uploader's file name: the uploadPaste mutation writes content to the upload folder using the client-supplied filename unsanitized, so ../ writes anywhere on disk (UploadPaste in core/views.py, save_file in core/helpers.py).

OWASP/crAPI.what: BOLA: GET /workshop/api/mechanic/mechanic_report?report_id= (a hidden endpoint linked from the contact_mechanic response) returns any user's mechanic report when the report id is changed (GetReportView in services/workshop/crapi/mechanic/views.py).

Mass assignment: a shadow PUT /workshop/api/shop/orders/{order_id} lets the user edit order properties (status, quantity), giving refunds for items never returned (OrderControlView.put in services/workshop/crapi/shop/views.py).
Negative quantity: POST /workshop/api/shop/orders accepts a negative quantity, which increases the available credit (OrderControlView.post in services/workshop/crapi/shop/views.py).

SQL injection to redeem an already-claimed coupon by modifying the database; the workshop coupon-redemption endpoint is POST /workshop/api/shop/apply_coupon (ApplyCouponView in services/workshop/crapi/shop/views.py). The docs do not name the endpoint; it comes from the OpenAPI spec and the coupon feature.

Prompt injection: text sent to the chatbot (POST /genai/ask in services/chatbot/src/chatbot/chat_api.py, agent in langgraph_agent.py) steers the LLM into returning content that is rendered client-side in the web chat widget (services/web/src/components/bot/).
LLM data leak: the chatbot can be prompted to reveal another user's credentials (services/chatbot).

Excessive LLM agency: the chatbot agent can be made to act on behalf of another user, for example placing an order, through its tool calls (services/chatbot/src/chatbot/langgraph_agent.py, services/chatbot/src/mcpserver/server.py).

Challenge 3: reset another user's password by brute-forcing the reset OTP (OTP handled by the Java identity service; v2/v3 check-otp endpoints).
Challenge 4: an endpoint leaks other users' sensitive information (endpoint not named in the docs).
Challenge 5: an endpoint leaks an internal property of a video (identity video API).
Challenge 6: layer-7 DoS through the contact mechanic feature (workshop).
Challenge 7: BFLA, deleting another user's video through the admin endpoint DELETE /identity/api/v2/admin/videos/{video_id} (identity service).
Challenge 10: updating internal video properties through PUT /identity/api/v2/user/videos/{video_id} (identity service).
Challenge 11: SSRF, making crAPI fetch www.google.com (endpoint not named in the docs).
Challenge 12: NoSQL injection to get free coupons, coupon validation at POST /community/api/v2/coupon/validate-coupon (community service).
Challenge 14: an endpoint that does not check authentication (endpoint not named in the docs).
Challenge 15: JWT forgery through algorithm confusion, an unchecked signature on the user dashboard, jku misuse and kid path traversal (identity service).
